scope:
Execute and price actual compiled actor clip reconstruction OFF/ON.

The timed entry includes full Part construction and Part::clip_strip. The
unchanged shared clipper exposes every prepared vertex/opacity byte then returns
zero, so clipping arithmetic, nonempty TA output and devices are excluded. The
same observed edge is used for both arms. Synthetic rigid, skinned and stride-6
source inputs cover near-crossing and far-depth strips, without game assets.
Warm/cold-I scheduling estimates assume perfect D-cache and a synthetic code
layout. Data load/store and 32-byte line visits are observed addresses, not
cache misses, bus traffic, console time or a whole-frame speedup estimate.

qualifications: Far-depth controls deliberately invoke clip_strip; ordinary rendering normally takes the existing fast strip path for these inputs.

The observed clipper returns zero. Unchanged clipper arithmetic and nonempty TA/device emission are excluded from target pricing; host tests use the real shared clipper and compare actual emitted bytes.
Synthetic fixture peak stack is 716 bytes OFF and 736 ON. Unique touched data lines rise by one; measured savings are repeated accesses, not a reduced total data footprint or measured cache misses.
The n=3 warm model regresses by 23 cycles for rigid/source6 and 14 for skin. Longer tested strips improve. No console, scene, FPS, whole-frame, or STRICT acceptance is claimed.
Fixture executable bytes rise 3192 to 3288; final production translation-unit and disabled identity checks are reported separately by build_controls.py.
